A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Calibration Tokens study. Their text, equations, six tables, eleven figures and supplementary material support reliable comparison, including verification that Appendix C was removed.

before.justification: v1 reports original ScanNet++ and KITTI-360 evaluations, ablations, computational measurements and qualitative results in Section 4 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including Tables 1–5 and the supplementary depth-estimation and reconstruction examples.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.2 retain the same layer-wise encoder tokens, frozen foundational models, synthetic fisheye inputs and self-supervised LogL1 objective computed after inverse projection into perspective space.

E1.justification: Both train using NYUv2, VOID, IRS, Hypersim and Waymo, and evaluate on ScanNet++ and KITTI-360. The applications discussed in the removed Appendix C were prospective, not additional evaluated tasks.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain MiDaS, DepthAnything and UniDepth without tokens, pretrained and retrained DepthAnyCamera, FoVA-Depth, and the same finetuning controls. Citation consolidation does not change comparator membership.

E3.justification: The model backbones, eight tokens per layer, 200K training mixture, 40K iterations, batch size, image resolutions and RMSE/δ1 metrics remain unchanged. The finetuning and supplementary experimental settings also match.

E4.justification: Both retain the token-placement and LogL1 ablations, embedding and attention visualizations, finetuning and computational analyses, and Appendix A's loss-frame, supervised-target and qualitative comparisons.

E5.justification: Both report point estimates without experimental run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice is added or removed.

E6.justification: All corresponding numerical results in Tables 1–5 and qualitative figures match. For example, UniDepth with tokens retains RMSE 0.244 on ScanNet++ and 2.040 on KITTI-360; Appendix A's supervised alternatives retain 0.242 and 1.994.

T1.justification: The mathematical setup, token definitions, distortion and projection equations, training objective and Table 6 metric definitions are unchanged. Neither version adds formal propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and Section 5 retain the same claims about fisheye adaptation, latent alignment, self-supervision, perspective-image compatibility and one token set serving indoor and outdoor settings.

C2.justification: v4 removes Appendix C's outlook on other perception tasks, multisensor applications and connections to continual learning. This removes peripheral applicability discussion; interpretations of the reported experiments and Section 5's dependence-on-backbone limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The implementation disclosures retain the same backbones, four NVIDIA 3090 GPUs, Adam parameters, learning rates, distortion ranges and dataset details. Both abstracts provide the same code-access link.

R1.justification: Deleting Appendix C removes the extended positioning across optical flow, segmentation, restoration, stereo, multisensor perception and continual learning, together with 33 distinct cited works, including RAFT, Segment Anything and Restormer. This substantially contracts the related-literature scope, although Section 2's core positioning remains. Eight further bibliography reductions consolidate duplicate entries for retained works.

P1.justification: v4 deletes supplementary Section C, adds Google gift funding to the acknowledgments, and consolidates duplicate bibliography entries with limited metadata edits. The scientific narrative and retained Appendices A–B otherwise preserve their wording and organization.

P2.justification: All figures and tables retain their content and organization. Minor table-width and text-spacing changes accompany bibliography reflow; deleting Appendix C also leaves the remaining Appendix B text more widely spaced on v4 page 15.

improvement.justification: v4 modestly improves editorial clarity by consolidating eight duplicate reference pairs and improves disclosure by acknowledging Google funding. Removing Appendix C trims an unevaluated applications outlook, with some loss of broader context. The experiments, reproducibility information and substantive limitations remain intact, making the net benefit limited.
